construct: tool error signal capture and provenance tracking — the ability of the signal pipeline to intercept a tool execution failure, create a signal record with non-empty provenance (identifying which tool failed and when), and make that signal queryable for downstream consumers like recentErrors.

input.description: A tool execution fails with a non-zero exit code. The signal pipeline must capture this event, record provenance information, and store it for later query.
setup: Tool execution returns non-zero exit code
Signal pipeline intercepts the error event
Signal pipeline writes a record with provenance field

expectedBehavior: Signal store contains exactly 1 tool error signal with provenance field non-null and including the tool name and invocation context. The main task continues executing without crash.
passCondition: signal_tool_error_count >= 1 AND signal_provenance_non_null_count >= 1 AND main_task_running == true
failureImplication: Tool errors are not captured by the signal pipeline, making it impossible to track, diagnose, or learn from tool failures.
relatedPaper: Meta-Harness: full traces >> scores-only (44% gap) — signal provenance is essential for trace-based evaluation.
regressionRisk: Changes to tool error event emission, signal store schema, or provenance field population could break signal capture.
